title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus: The Unknown Threat Our Children Face — Dr Azanna Ahmad Kamar - CodeBlue

analysis.time: Publication date: 17 July 2026. Event timing: RSV is described as present year-round with a typical peak from September to December, extending into January the following year (N6).
analysis.location_and_population: Malaysia; focus on infants aged six months and below, including premature infants and those with congenital disorders or other comorbidities (N11, N13). Healthy full-term infants are also affected (N14).
analysis.event: An opinion article by Dr Azanna Ahmad Kamar, a consultant neonatologist and paediatrician, highlights Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) as a significant but under-recognized threat to children, particularly infants, due to its high contagiousness and potential for severe outcomes (N4, N5, N7, N9, N10).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: In Malaysia, RSV accounts for 81.3% of viral respiratory tract infections (RTI) in children aged six months and below (N11). Among infected children below two years old, 84.5% result in hospitalization (N19). Severe cases may require urgent breathing support or ICU care (N20). Local studies report mechanical ventilation rates between 2.5% and 6.9% (N21). RSV is associated with long-term respiratory complications, including a 12-fold higher risk of developing asthma (N28).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Preventive measures emphasized include breastfeeding, good hygiene practices (handwashing, face masks), avoiding close contact with unwell individuals, and keeping unwell children out of school or childcare (N31, N32, N33, N34, N35). Childcare facilities are advised to avoid overcrowding, maintain clean and disinfected surfaces, and ensure smoke-free environments (N36, N37). Prevention options include maternal vaccination and childhood immunization with monoclonal antibodies (N39).

analysis.brief_en: A leading Malaysian paediatrician has warned that Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) poses a serious but often overlooked threat to infants, with two-thirds of babies experiencing their first infection before age one. In Malaysia, RSV accounts for over 80% of viral respiratory infections in infants under six months and triggers hospitalization in 84.5% of cases under two years, including many previously healthy full-term babies. Severe outcomes may require intensive care, while long-term complications such as asthma and recurrent wheezing are significantly more likely. The virus circulates year-round, peaking from September to December, and spreads efficiently through droplets. Experts urge parents to adopt preventive measures like breastfeeding, rigorous hygiene, and avoiding contact with sick individuals, while advocating for maternal vaccination and monoclonal antibody immunization to reduce the burden on families and healthcare systems.

title: newsGP - RSV tops most notified respiratory virus - Royal Australian College of General Practitioners (RACGP)

analysis.time: Publication date: 15 July 2026. Event period: first half of 2026 (January–June 2026).
analysis.location_and_population: Australia, national scope. Affected groups: children younger than five years (46% of confirmed RSV cases), adults aged 75+ years, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people aged 60+, and people with medical risk factors for severe RSV disease.
analysis.event: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) has become the most notified respiratory virus in Australia during the first half of 2026, surpassing influenza and COVID-19 notifications. Reported by the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners (RACGP) via the Immunisation Foundation of Australia (IFA) mid-winter report card.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 83,678 confirmed RSV cases (45% of notifications for the three main respiratory viruses), 51,655 COVID-19 cases, and 49,785 influenza cases in the first half of 2026. Children under five account for 46% of RSV cases. IFA projects >127,000 RSV cases by end of winter 2026. Reduced newborn hospital admissions by almost half in the first year of the infant RSV immunisation program. Approximately 1 million Australians aged 75+ remain unvaccinated despite free eligibility under the National Immunisation Program (NIP).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: National Immunisation Program (NIP) provides free RSV vaccination for eligible cohorts: pregnant women (28–36 weeks), adults ≥75 years, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people ≥60 years, adults ≥60 with risk factors, and infants up to eight months (if mother unvaccinated) plus at-risk infants/children via state programs. Vaccine cost ($300) outside NIP eligibility is cited as a barrier. 64% of adults ≥75 unaware RSV and influenza vaccines can be co-administered. Vaccine shortages reported in some jurisdictions. Ongoing GP-led awareness campaigns to improve vaccine uptake and RSV recognition.

analysis.brief_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) has overtaken influenza and COVID-19 to become Australia’s most notified respiratory virus in the first half of 2026, with 83,678 confirmed cases reported by the Immunisation Foundation of Australia (IFA). Children under five account for 46% of cases, while adults aged 75 and older represent a major immunisation gap—around one million remain unvaccinated despite free eligibility under the National Immunisation Program (NIP). The IFA projects more than 127,000 RSV cases by winter’s end. Public health experts highlight cost barriers outside NIP eligibility and low awareness of co-administration with influenza vaccines as key drivers of under-vaccination. Meanwhile, the infant RSV immunisation program has cut newborn hospital admissions by nearly half in its first year, underscoring the vaccine’s impact. GPs are urged to raise awareness as vaccine shortages and hesitancy persist.

title: RSV overtakes flu as Australia’s top winter virus - Nine.com.au

analysis.time: The report was published on 2026-07-15, with the event occurring during the mid-winter period of 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The event is occurring in Australia, affecting older Australians aged 75 and over, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people aged 60 and over, and infants.
analysis.event: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) has overtaken influenza as the most dominant winter illness in Australia, with over 83,000 cases recorded this year. The Immunisation Foundation of Australia (IFA) reported this shift, noting that RSV vaccinations are now free for older Australians.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Australia has recorded over 83,000 RSV cases this year, with an average of 890 daily notifications. The IFA projects around 127,000 cases by the end of the season. RSV can cause severe respiratory illnesses, hospitalisations, and lasting health declines in older adults.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The IFA and health experts are urging older Australians to get vaccinated. The RSV vaccine, which became free a few months ago, is highly effective in reducing hospitalisations. The IFA and Australian Medical Association are calling for immediate action to increase vaccination rates.

analysis.brief_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) has surpassed influenza as Australia's most prevalent winter illness, according to a mid-winter report by the Immunisation Foundation of Australia (IFA). With over 83,000 cases recorded this year and an average of 890 daily notifications, Australia is on track to reach around 127,000 cases by the end of the season. The IFA highlights a significant gap in RSV vaccination coverage, with only 722,530 older Australians vaccinated compared to 1.76 million who received the flu shot. Health experts emphasize the importance of RSV vaccination, which has been shown to reduce hospitalisations by over 85% and is now free for older Australians. The Australian Medical Association urges unprotected individuals to contact healthcare professionals immediately to maximize winter protection.

analysis.time: The article was published on July 16, 2026. The event date is not specified in the supplied evidence.
analysis.location_and_population: The location is not specified in the supplied evidence. The population affected is not specified in the supplied evidence.
analysis.event: The article discusses the transformation of RSV surveillance in clinical research through whole-genome sequencing. It is reported by Cerba Research and reviewed by Louis Castel. The event is confirmed as a scientific advancement in RSV surveillance.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The scale, impact, and risk are not specified in the supplied evidence.

analysis.brief_en: The article published on July 16, 2026, by News-Medical discusses the transformative impact of whole-genome sequencing on RSV surveillance in clinical research. Authored by Cerba Research and reviewed by Louis Castel, the piece highlights the use of advanced sequencing techniques to monitor respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) strains, including HRSV-A and HRSV-B. The methodology involves the use of subgroup-specific primers and a two-primer-pool multiplex PCR-tiling approach to cover the entire viral genome. The study achieved successful amplification of HRSV-A/B ATCC strains, nasal wash isolates, and strain dilution replicates, yielding high genome coverage and low sequencing errors. The results demonstrate the potential of these assays for large-scale viral genomic surveillance and the evaluation of drug-resistant mutations in new antiviral therapies. Cerba Research, a leading specialty laboratory services provider, emphasizes the importance of accurate and timely characterization of HRSV genomes for effective surveillance and monitoring.

title: The mRNA-1345 RSV vaccine candidate - Moderna Inc. bets on older adults - Ad-hoc-news.de

analysis.time: Publication date: 18 July 2026 at 10:12 (event date not specified; product development and trial data described as interim or planned).
analysis.location_and_population: Global trial sites (approximately 37,000 participants worldwide); target population: adults aged 60 years and older; regulatory submissions planned in the United States, Europe, and other markets.
analysis.event: reports interim Phase 3 trial results for the investigational mRNA-1345 RSV vaccine candidate in adults ≥60 years, describing efficacy and safety; regulatory submissions underway or planned; product positioned for seasonal pre-RSV-peak administration.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Phase 3 trial (ConquerRSV) enrolled roughly 37,000 participants worldwide; interim efficacy against RSV-associated lower respiratory tract disease with ≥2 symptoms: approximately 83.7%; safety profile consistent with other adult vaccines, with mostly mild to moderate, transient adverse events; serious related adverse events rare; no new safety signals reported; potential to reduce RSV-associated hospitalizations in older adults with comorbidities.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Investigational status; regulatory submissions (FDA, EMA, and others) underway or planned; manufacturing and cold-chain logistics being prepared; single-dose schedule designed for seasonal deployment; combination vaccine prospects under investigation; unresolved: final regulatory decisions, real-world effectiveness, and market uptake.

analysis.brief_en: Moderna Inc. has reported interim Phase 3 data showing that its investigational mRNA-1345 vaccine candidate is approximately 83.7% effective against laboratory-confirmed RSV-associated lower respiratory tract disease with at least two symptoms in adults aged 60 and older. The ConquerRSV trial enrolled roughly 37,000 participants globally and evaluated a single 50 μg dose administered before the RSV season. Safety findings were consistent with other adult vaccines, with mostly mild to moderate, transient adverse events and rare serious related events. Moderna has initiated or prepared regulatory submissions in the United States, Europe, and other markets, positioning mRNA-1345 for seasonal use ahead of winter peaks. The company is also exploring combination respiratory vaccines that could integrate RSV with influenza and COVID-19 antigens in future formulations.
